newsitem.title: IVORY COAST: Sierra Leone peace deal agreed, signing Saturday.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone peace deal agreed, signing Saturday.

text.p: Sierra Leone's government and rebels have struck a peace deal to end more than five years of civil war and a formal accord will be signed on Saturday in Ivory Coast's commercial capital Abidjan.

A senior Ivorian official said on Friday that rebel leader Foday Sankoh was among negotiators from the two sides who finalised the deal on Thursday night in Abidjan in the presence of Ivorian mediators.

"The signing of this accord will take place on Saturday in the presence of the Ivorian president and his Sierra Leone counterpart," the official told Reuters, adding that heads of states of neighbouring countries had been invited.
Sources close to the talks said Ivorian "perseverance" had brought the rebel delegation round to a conciliatory position.

Sankoh, who in 1991 launched the country's civil war that killed at least 10,000 people, returned to Ivory Coast from Sierra Leone on Wednesday after talks with his fighters in the bush, during which he sought a mandate to sign.
Before leaving, he had been in Ivory Coast since March.

Sierra Leone had been expecting the signing in Ivory Coast on Friday. State radio there said on Thursday that the government of President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah was calling for national celebrations to welcome the return of peace.

Traditional rulers from rebel-held areas in the east said on Wednesday Sankoh's fighters had demanded international monitors to guarantee their safety and disbanding of civil defence units made up of Kamajor traditional hunters before any signing.

The Kamajors had been attacking rebel positions across the nation and the truce extended by Tejan Kabbah and Sankoh in talks in Ivory Coast in April had looked more and more fragile prior to the latest peace developments.
Kabbah, who took office in March after multi-party elections ended four years of army rule, earlier threatened the military option if Sankoh did not agree to peace by December 1.
The civil war in Sierra Leone, a former British colony, has killed at least 10,000 people, according to official estimates.
The rebels launched a low-level guerrilla campaign from the border with Liberia in March 1991. A 1992 army coup failed to bring a military solution.
Rebels who held 17 foreign hostages for months disrupted the country's mainstay bauxite, rutile, diamonds and gold mining industry by forcing foreign-owned mines to close or cut back.
By early 1995 rebels were attacking close to the capital. The government brought in mercenaries from South African firm Executive Outcomes and retook the initiative.
Differences over the presence of foreign troops -- Nigerians, Guineans and the South Africans -- had blocked a deal.
